reasons: Composio has no managed OAuth app for LinkedIn Ads. Its toolkit page says so directly, and its managed-auth directory lists LinkedIn Ads under 'Bring your own OAuth app' while plain LinkedIn is Composio-managed.

LinkedIn only switches on the ads scopes (r_ads, rw_ads, r_ads_reporting) for an app after it approves that app's Advertising API access request. Approval is tied to one app, one company and one LinkedIn Page, so you need an app of your own that LinkedIn has vetted.

On the Development tier, one app can edit at most 5 ad accounts, and those accounts are listed on the app itself. Composio does not say why it offers no managed app, but a shared app would hit that cap almost at once.

verdict.summary: Gated. You cannot make a single ads API call until LinkedIn approves your app for the Advertising API. That approval includes identity vetting of your company (business email, legally registered organization, website, privacy policy, verified LinkedIn Page), and LinkedIn can refuse it at its discretion. Agents that only read reporting data can go live on the Development tier once that first approval lands. Agents that create or edit campaigns in more than 5 ad accounts need a second Standard tier review, which LinkedIn says can take up to 30 business days.

timeToTesting.label: About 1-8 weeks: a few hours of setup, then LinkedIn's Advertising API review, which has no published timeline

timeToProduction.label: Read-only agents: live once the Development tier is approved (about 1-8 weeks). Editing more than 5 ad accounts: Standard tier on top of that, up to 30 business days after you submit a demo video

verdict.mainBlocker: LinkedIn's Advertising API access review, with identity vetting of your organization, before any ads scope works at all. If your agent writes campaigns for many customers, the Standard tier review and its demo video come after that.

stages.name: Create the app and verify it with your LinkedIn Page

duration.label: 30-60 min if you are the Page super admin; up to 30 days if you wait on someone else to click the link

limits: The app stays tied to the LinkedIn Page you pick. It cannot be moved to another Page later.
The Page verification link expires after 30 days.
The app name must not include any part of the LinkedIn or Microsoft names or logos, or the access request is rejected.

steps.title: Make sure your company has a real LinkedIn Page
steps.detail: LinkedIn's quick start begins with creating a LinkedIn Page for your company. Use your real company's Page: LinkedIn rejects requests where the Page belongs to a different organization, and says not to use a fake or test Page. The app is permanently tied to this Page, so pick it carefully.
steps.humanReason: Creating or administering a company Page needs a signed-in LinkedIn member with rights to that Page.

steps.title: Create the developer app
steps.detail: In the Developer Portal, create a new app. Enter the app name (this is what your users see on the consent screen), the LinkedIn Page URL and a logo, then accept the legal terms. Keep LinkedIn and Microsoft names out of the app name.
steps.humanReason: Requires signing in to LinkedIn and accepting LinkedIn's API terms on behalf of your company.

preparedValues.label: App name
preparedValues.value: Your product's name, with no 'Linked', 'In', 'LinkedIn' or 'Microsoft' in it

preparedValues.label: LinkedIn Page
preparedValues.value: Your own company's Page URL, the same company named in the access request

steps.title: Get the app verified by your Page's super admin
steps.detail: Open the app's Settings tab, click Verify, then Generate URL. Send that URL to a super admin of your LinkedIn Page. The app is verified once they open it and approve. The link is valid for 30 days.
steps.humanReason: Only a super admin of the LinkedIn Page can approve the association.

preparedValues.label: Message to your Page super admin
preparedValues.value: Hi, I've created a LinkedIn developer app for <product> so our AI agent can manage and report on our LinkedIn ad accounts. LinkedIn needs a super admin of our company Page to confirm the app belongs to us. Could you open this link and approve it? It expires in 30 days: <verification URL>

steps.title: Add Composio's redirect URL
steps.detail: On the app's Auth tab, add Composio's redirect URI under Authorized redirect URLs. Copy it from your Composio dashboard when you create the LinkedIn Ads auth config. Composio's own guidance says to register the exact callback its current auth-config flow shows, without guessing between older versions or adding a trailing slash. LinkedIn needs an absolute HTTPS URL with no # in it and ignores query parameters.

preparedValues.label: Redirect URL
preparedValues.value: Copy from Composio: Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > LinkedIn Ads > OAuth2

stages.name: Apply for the Advertising API (Development tier)

duration.label: About 1-8 weeks. No published timeline; reports range from several business days to several weeks

limits: None of the ads scopes work until this request is approved.
You must finish the vetting survey within 21 days of it appearing, or the request is closed as Insufficient Details.
Development tier: read data for any ad account the connected user administers, create 1 test ad account through the API, and edit at most 5 ad accounts, which must be added to the app by ID.
Approval is at LinkedIn's discretion, even when you meet every listed requirement.

steps.title: Check your use case against LinkedIn's restrictions
steps.detail: Before applying, read LinkedIn's restricted uses page. Member data must not be used for ad targeting, building audience lists, enriching a CRM or sales prospecting. Social activity data may be stored for at most 48 hours and most profile data for 24 hours. One individual profile must not be used to manage many customers' ad accounts. The Advertising API also cannot be used to enhance Sign In with LinkedIn or collect member profile data.

steps.title: Request the Advertising API on the Products tab
steps.detail: On the app's Products tab, find the Advertising API and request access. LinkedIn then opens an access request form. Its published prerequisites for Marketing API access ask for a business email address (personal addresses fail), your organization's legal name, registered address and website, and a verified company Page. LinkedIn checks the email, the organization, the website and the privacy policy during identity vetting.
steps.humanReason: The form is a set of declarations about your company, and the business email has to be verified from your own inbox.

preparedValues.label: Business email
preparedValues.value: An address on your company's domain, the same domain as the website you list

preparedValues.label: Privacy policy URL
preparedValues.value: A live privacy policy on your company website that covers data from LinkedIn ad accounts

steps.title: Write the use-case description
steps.detail: Vague or non-compliant descriptions are a reported rejection reason, and LinkedIn lists 'Unapproved Use Case' and 'Incomplete Access Request Form' among its denial reasons. Describe an ads management or reporting use case in plain terms: who your users are, which of their own ad accounts the agent touches, and what it reads and writes. Your agent can draft this for you to edit.

preparedValues.label: Draft use-case description
preparedValues.value: <Company> builds <product>, an AI assistant for B2B marketing teams. Advertisers connect their own LinkedIn ad accounts with OAuth. The assistant reads campaign, creative and analytics data (r_ads, r_ads_reporting) so marketers can ask questions such as 'which campaigns had the lowest cost per lead last week' and get reports. With the user's approval it also creates and edits campaign groups, campaigns and lead gen forms (rw_ads) in ad accounts where the user holds a Campaign Manager or Account Manager role. We act only on accounts the authenticated member administers. We do not use member data for targeting, audience building, CRM enrichment or prospecting, and we follow LinkedIn's data storage limits.

steps.title: Answer follow-ups within 21 days
steps.detail: The request moves through Access Form Review, Identity Vetting and App Review. If reviewers need more, they write to your registered business email. Unanswered requests and surveys left unsubmitted for 21 days are marked Insufficient Details. Since May 2025 a Reapply button reloads the form for those cases. Other rejections mean creating a new app.
steps.humanReason: The replies come to your business inbox and speak for your company.

steps.title: Map your ad accounts to the app
steps.detail: Once approved, the Advertising API scopes appear on the Auth tab. If your agent will create or edit anything, copy each nine-digit ad account ID from Campaign Manager and add it under Products > View Ad Accounts. On the Development tier, edits to accounts not added here fail with 403. Read-only calls do not need this.
steps.humanReason: Inside your signed-in Developer Portal and Campaign Manager.

stages.name: Connect it in Composio and test
limits: Access tokens last 60 days. Refresh tokens last 365 days from the first consent and are not extended when used, so every user has to reconnect at least once a year.
Changing the requested scopes invalidates the user's earlier access tokens, and users must consent again.
Daily rate limits per app and per member are not published. They reset at midnight UTC and show in the app's Analytics tab after your first call to an endpoint.

steps.title: Create the LinkedIn Ads auth config in Composio
steps.detail: Create an OAuth2 auth config for LinkedIn Ads with your own Client ID and Client Secret from the Auth tab. Request only scopes that now appear on your app's Auth tab: LinkedIn rejects the whole sign-in if any requested scope is not available to the app. Composio's public docs do not list the toolkit's default scopes, so compare them with your Auth tab before you save.

preparedValues.label: Add for campaign and lead form management
Add for Page admin and Page posts tools

steps.title: Connect your own LinkedIn account and run a read tool
steps.detail: Start a connection, approve LinkedIn's consent screen and run a read tool such as Search Ad Accounts. The member who connects must hold a role on the ad account (for example Account Manager or Campaign Manager), or reads come back empty and writes fail.
steps.humanReason: You approve the consent screen with your own LinkedIn account.

steps.title: Check the API version your calls use
steps.detail: LinkedIn's Marketing APIs need a Linkedin-Version header (YYYYMM) on every call. Each monthly version is supported for at least one year, and calls with a missing or sunset version fail. Version 202511 sunsets on November 16, 2026. Composio's toolkit sets the calls, so this is mostly something to watch when tools start failing after a sunset date.

stages.name: Standard tier (only to edit more than 5 ad accounts)

duration.label: Not needed for read-only agents. Otherwise up to 30 business days after you file the ticket, plus time to record the demo

limits: Requests for data or analytics use cases alone are rejected, because reads already have no account limit.
LinkedIn may decline the upgrade even if you meet the minimum requirements.

steps.title: Record a demo video
steps.detail: Record your product creating, editing and optimizing LinkedIn campaigns through the API. If you need to create ads in more than 5 ad accounts, show that clearly in the video. Share it as a Google Drive or Microsoft SharePoint link.
steps.humanReason: The demo has to show your working product with a real signed-in session.

preparedValues.label: Demo script
preparedValues.value: 1. Connect a LinkedIn account through the product. 2. Ask the agent to create a campaign group and a campaign with targeting and budget. 3. Edit the campaign's budget and status. 4. Show an optimization action based on analytics. 5. Repeat in a second customer's ad account to show multi-account management.

steps.title: File the upgrade request as a support ticket
steps.detail: Standard tier is requested through a ticket on the Developer Support Portal, not a button in the app. Give your Client ID, the business use case and the video link.
steps.humanReason: A request made on behalf of your company.

preparedValues.label: Ticket description
preparedValues.value: We request an upgrade of our app (Client ID <id>) from Development to Standard tier for the Advertising API. <Product> lets advertisers manage their own LinkedIn campaigns through an AI assistant: it creates, edits and optimizes campaign groups, campaigns and creatives in ad accounts where the connected member holds a manager role. Our customers manage more than 5 ad accounts in total, which the Development tier does not allow. Demo video: <link>.

requirements.title: A real, verified LinkedIn Page for your company
requirements.detail: The app must be associated with your company's Page and verified by its super admin. The Page must belong to the same organization as the request, and the association is permanent.

requirements.title: A legally registered organization, business email, website and privacy policy
requirements.detail: LinkedIn's identity vetting checks each of these, and failing any one is a listed rejection reason. Personal email addresses do not pass.

requirements.title: A supported ads management or reporting use case
requirements.detail: Member data cannot be used for targeting, audience building, CRM enrichment or prospecting, and the Advertising API cannot be used to enhance Sign In with LinkedIn.

requirements.title: Users reconnect once a year
requirements.detail: Refresh tokens expire 365 days after the first consent, however often they are used, and LinkedIn can revoke tokens at any time. LinkedIn's docs disagree on whether every approved Advertising API app gets refresh tokens at all; without them, access tokens end after 60 days.

requirements.title: Separate LinkedIn products for some Composio tools
requirements.detail: The toolkit includes tools for DMP segments and conversion rules. On LinkedIn's side those sit in the Matched Audiences API (rw_dmp_segments) and Conversions API (rw_conversions), each with its own application. Reading lead responses needs the Lead Sync API, while creating lead gen forms is covered by rw_ads. Community Management API features need a separate app, because that product must be the only one on its app.

blockers.title: Ads scopes missing or 'Invalid scope'
blockers.symptom: The consent screen fails with an invalid scope error, or the Auth tab shows no r_ads or rw_ads.
blockers.fix: The Advertising API is not approved yet, or the auth config asks for a scope from a product you don't have. Check the Products tab status and request only the scopes listed on the Auth tab.

blockers.title: Access request rejected
blockers.symptom: The Products tab shows Access denied with a reason such as Fail Email Verification, Fail Organization Verification, Invalid Company Page or Unapproved Use Case.
blockers.fix: For Insufficient Details, use the Reapply button. For identity vetting denials, file a Vetting Appeal through the developer support contact form. For other rejections, fix the cause and create a new app.

blockers.title: 403 when creating or editing in an ad account
blockers.symptom: Reads work, but creating or updating campaigns returns 403.
blockers.fix: On the Development tier, add the ad account ID under Products > View Ad Accounts (at most 5). Also check that the connected member has a manager role on that account. For more accounts, apply for Standard tier.

blockers.title: Redirect URL mismatch
blockers.symptom: LinkedIn returns 'Redirect_uri doesn't match' before the consent screen.
blockers.fix: Make the redirect URL on the Auth tab identical to the one in your Composio auth config. Copy it from the Composio dashboard, with no trailing slash.

blockers.title: Every connection breaks a year after it was made
blockers.symptom: Tools fail with an invalid or expired refresh token, about 365 days after the user first connected.
blockers.fix: Expected behavior: LinkedIn's refresh tokens have a fixed one-year life. Prompt users to reconnect before the date.

blockers.title: 429 errors across many users
blockers.symptom: Tool calls fail with 429 Too Many Requests until midnight UTC.
blockers.fix: The app or member daily limit was reached. Check the limits in the app's Analytics tab and cut call volume; LinkedIn emails admins at 75% of the app quota.

blockers.title: Calls fail after a version sunset
blockers.symptom: Errors about a missing or deprecated Linkedin-Version header.
blockers.fix: Update to a supported version. Each version lasts at least a year; check the toolkit version in Composio if tools start failing after a sunset date.

claims.text: An August 2026 guide from a vendor of a LinkedIn API alternative claims Marketing API approval realistically takes 4-8 weeks on the fast path and 3-4 months on average, and that rejections are common and rarely explained. It does not cite first-hand cases and the vendor sells an alternative.

sources.title: ConnectSafely: LinkedIn API 2026 guide (Aug 2026)
sources.quote: approval is realistically 4-8 weeks on the fast path and 3-4 months on average

claims.text: A unified-API vendor's guide (May 2026, updated October 2026) reports that incomplete company information on the app is a common rejection reason and that approval is not instant.

sources.title: Unified.to: How to get your LinkedIn Ads API key
sources.quote: Incomplete company info is a common rejection reason, so complete this fully.

claims.text: Estimate: app creation, Page verification (when you are the super admin), redirect setup and the Composio connection take under an hour each, based on the number of console steps; the overall 1-8 week testing range adds the unpublished review wait reported by third parties. Not timed in a real attempt.

Estimate: Composio does not state why LinkedIn Ads has no managed app. The likely reasons are that Advertising API access is vetted per app and company, and that a Development tier app can edit only 5 mapped ad accounts.
Composio's public LinkedIn Ads docs do not list the scopes the toolkit requests by default.
The Community Management API must be the only product on its developer app; apps with other products (such as the Ads API) need a separate app for it.

sources.title: LinkedIn: API Partner Support
sources.quote: The Community Management API requires that it be the only product associated with a developer application due to legal and security constraints.

claims.text: Composio's LinkedIn credentials guide has you create the app with a name, company Page URL and logo, accept the legal terms, copy the Client ID and Secret from the Auth tab and add the redirect URI there; it shows https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback as the redirect URI.

sources.title: Composio: How to create OAuth2 credentials for LinkedIn

claims.text: rw_ads is restricted to ad accounts where the member holds ACCOUNT_BILLING_ADMIN, ACCOUNT_MANAGER, CAMPAIGN_MANAGER or CREATIVE_MANAGER, and members need the matching Page and ad account roles to read or act on them.

sources.title: LinkedIn: Increasing Access
sources.quote: Restricted to ad accounts where the authenticated member has one of the following roles: ACCOUNT_BILLING_ADMIN, ACCOUNT_MANAGER, CAMPAIGN_MANAGER, CREATIVE_MANAGER.
